input.quote: Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice.
input.rationale: Section 8.2 auto-renews each Order Form for twelve months but requires 180 days' advance non-renewal notice. That is double the 90-day walk-away threshold and triple the 60-day fallback, so it fails the fallback on a material term: we would have to decide on renewal six months out. The 12-month renewal term itself is fine (no multi-year auto-renewal). Pricing is not an issue — Section 8.3 already caps renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice and no increase on prepaid periods, which meets the preferred position. The only gap beyond the notice window was the absence of a Vendor renewal reminder, which we have folded into the same edit rather than raising separately.

ops.oldText: Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice.
ops.newText: Each Order Form renews for successive twelve-month terms unless either Party gives thirty days' advance written notice before the end of the then-current term. Vendor shall notify Customer of the upcoming renewal at least sixty days before the renewal date.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We shortened the non-renewal notice window from 180 days to 30 days and added a 60-day renewal reminder, consistent with our playbook position that renewals must be easy to exit; we can accept up to 60 days' notice as a fallback.
proposal.summary: Shorten renewal opt-out notice to 30 days and add Vendor renewal reminder.
